SMTO-GWT-0051 — SMTO couldn't find the Gateway computer by its name

GUID: 7233ea06-3158-40b2-a6c9-44f36ef5846c
Slug: gateway-dns
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • SMTO looked up the Gateway computer's name on the network and got no address back, so it couldn't connect. This request was not sent to the Gateway.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Edit for this Gateway, and check that Host is spelled exactly right, with no http:// and no slashes. One wrong letter in the name means the network can't find the computer.
  2. If the Gateway computer is on a work or private network, make sure the computer running SMTO is connected to that network too, for example that its VPN is on. Names on a private network can usually only be looked up from inside that network.
  3. If the name still isn't found, ask the Gateway's manager for its IP address, enter that in Host, save, and select Check connection. An IP address skips the name lookup that is failing.
  4. If an earlier step in the same Task was interrupted, first check whether it already finished. Then send your request again. This request never reached the Gateway, but an earlier interrupted step might have run.

What success looks like

  • Check connection shows the Gateway as connected, and your request reaches it without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Gateway's Host name, to the person who manages your network or the Gateway computer. Don't delete and re-add the Gateway; the name lookup will fail the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Connecting to the selected inbound Gateway failed with socket.gaierror (hostname resolution) before any request bytes were sent.

What this means

  • Connection setup raised socket.gaierror before application request bytes could be sent; the structured category preserves a hostname-resolution failure. This connection failure occurs before application request transmission. That boundary applies to this request and does not settle any previous operation.

Why this can happen

  • Connection setup raised socket.gaierror before application request bytes could be sent; the structured category preserves a hostname-resolution failure.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the selected host spelling and controller-side name resolution; no listener response is established by this error.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway record's Host (Settings › Setup › Gateways › Edit) and try resolving it from the Server host (for example getent hosts or nslookup). Correct the hostname, fix DNS or VPN on the Server host, or use a reachable IP address. This request never left the Server, but earlier operations on the same Gateway keep their own recorded outcome.
  • Correct the selected Gateway hostname or the controller DNS configuration.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended hostname resolves to the expected address and the connection passes identity checks.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • This connection failure occurs before application request transmission. That boundary applies to this request and does not settle any previous operation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
